topic: Bone health assessment in older people

audits.title: 98 Bone health: managed correctly? A clinical audit
audits.standard: 2021 UK National Osteoporosis Guideline Group strong recommendations
audits.setting: Geriatric assessment and treatment clinic, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Only 25% investigated, treated and prescribed bone health medication as per NOGG 2021.

audits.other_findings: Comorbidity, mobility and frailty history well completed and follow-up well documented, but referrals to allied health practitioners lacking.
audits.citation: Rust G. 98 Bone health: managed correctly? A clinical audit. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.111.

audits.title: 242 Optimising bone health assessment and management in Parkinson’s Disease: a closed loop quality improvement project
audits.setting: Weekly Parkinson's Disease Interdisciplinary Clinic, age-related day hospital, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: 36% had known osteoporosis, of whom 33% were not on treatment; 27% had a previous fragility fracture, 33% of these not on treatment; 27% had a DXA scan.

audits.intervention: 'Bone health' section added to the clinic proforma

cycle2.result: Suboptimal bone health management warranting intervention identified in 50%; 25% started calcium/cholecalciferol; 8.3% restarted denosumab; 8.3% counselled on denosumab; 8.3% repeat DXA booked; 33% had a DXA.

audits.other_findings: 42% were unsure of their osteoporosis diagnosis in cycle 2; over 66% had a history of falls.
audits.citation: Gallagher C, Killeen E, McDonough A, Cronin A, Latoza P, Baldestamon G, et al.. 242 Optimising bone health assessment and management in Parkinson’s Disease: a closed loop quality improvement project. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_3). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad156.198.

audits.title: 2999 An audit of the impact of bone health assessment in residential home patients
audits.setting: Enhanced Health in Care Homes team, five residential homes, Whittington Hospital, London

cycle1.result: Before CGA, 37% of residents with high or very high FRAX score were on appropriate bone protection.

audits.intervention: Comprehensive geriatric assessment with FRAX and management plan by the new EHCH team.

cycle2.result: After EHCH CGA, 85% on appropriate bone protection; 100% (183) had bone health assessment including FRAX.

audits.other_findings: Largest improvement in one home was from 0% to 83%.
audits.citation: Evans S. 2999 An audit of the impact of bone health assessment in residential home patients. Age and Ageing. 2025;54(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf133.021.

audits.title: 3589 Embedding FRAX scoring into the comprehensive geriatric assessment following an inpatient audit
audits.standard: NICE criteria for bone health assessment
audits.setting: Colwell Ward, Isle of Wight NHS Trust, one-day inpatient audit

cycle1.result: 100% met NICE criteria for BHA; BHA mentioned in 2/30 (6.7%); FRAX calculated in 0; vitamin D checked 14/30 (46.7%); calcium 28/30 (93.3%); vitamin D and calcium prescribed 17/30 (56.7%); ARM started in 2/30 (6.7%).

audits.intervention: FRAX scoring included in the CGA piloted by the acute frailty team.
audits.other_findings: Re-audit recommended after full CGA implementation.
audits.citation: Soma A, Jones L, Clift E. 3589 Embedding FRAX scoring into the comprehensive geriatric assessment following an inpatient audit. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.004.

audits.title: 3724 An audit of inpatient falls—are we adequately addressing bone health?
audits.standard: National Osteoporosis Guideline Group: FRAX to estimate 10-year fracture risk and guide bone protection; NICE CG161; Trust post-fall assessment guidance
audits.setting: Sherwood Forest Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (Kings Mill Hospital); inpatients who fell, identified via DATIX

cycle1.result: Falls assessment sheet completed in over 80%; FRAX calculated in only 33.3%. Of those with FRAX, 60% intermediate, 20% high and 10% very high risk; only 50% of high-risk patients received oral bisphosphonates. Retrospective FRAX in those not assessed showed 60% very high risk.

audits.other_findings: Calcium and vitamin D checks were done more often than FRAX but still below optimal; renal impairment limited bisphosphonate eligibility. Falls Alert Stickers with checkboxes and QR code, a revised post-falls proforma with a bone health section, and clinician education were introduced.
audits.citation: Ahmed A. 3724 An audit of inpatient falls—are we adequately addressing bone health?. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/ageing/afaf368.022.

audits.title: An audit on the assessment and management of osteoporosis in a Parkinson's and related diseases clinic in Australia.
audits.setting: Parkinson's and related diseases neurology clinic, Macquarie University, Sydney

cycle1.result: 78 patients over 50 had risk factors; 26 already managed appropriately; only 12/52 (23%) remaining at-risk patients directed to GP screening, 77% (40/52) without guidance.

audits.other_findings: Recommend referring at-risk patients to their GP for bone health screening.
audits.citation: Amarasekera NN, Taylor J, Coppin C, Lewis SJG. An audit on the assessment and management of osteoporosis in a Parkinson's and related diseases clinic in Australia. J Neurol. 2025;272(2):139. doi:10.1007/s00415-024-12752-z. PMID: 39812661.
